summary: Blind A/B judge panel: which proposed dev-flow shape better fits each task situation

votes.reason: The situation has an unknown root cause (a subtle race in shared pool code), so Flow X's dedicated analyze:diagnose step after gather-context is exactly the right fit; Flow Y omits diagnosis and jumps from context to plan, under-built for a cause that must be analyzed before fixing.

The situation states the cause is unknown and is a subtle race condition in shared pool code; Flow X's dedicated analyze:diagnose step forces root-cause analysis before planning, which Flow Y skips, risking a plan built on an unconfirmed cause.

The explicit diagnose step decides it: the failure is intermittent with an unknown cause and a masking trap (a test retry would hide the real ConnectionPool race), so pinning root cause before planning is exactly what this situation requires. Flow Y folds diagnosis into plan and risks jumping to a fix shape before the race is understood.

The plan step in Flow Y is the deciding step: the investigation shows a fully-paved path (one Serializer + one registry line against a documented interface, a shared button, an existing golden-file test pattern), so there is no design decision for a plan step to resolve, making Flow Y over-built. Flow X's gather-context, act, verify, close is the right fit.

Both flows are identical except Y adds a plan:plan(compose) step. Investigation showed the work is a mechanical, well-scoped implementation against a documented interface (one Serializer plus one registry line, shared button, existing golden-file test pattern), so the dedicated planning step in Y is a wasted step and the leaner X fits better.

The plan step in Flow Y is the only difference and it adds no value here: investigation already reduced the task to implementing one documented Serializer interface plus one registry line with an existing button and golden-test pattern, so there is no design decision left to plan.

The task explicitly asks to first decide whether the migration is the right call, which is exactly what X's diagnose step provides and Y omits; X's reviewer step also fits an auth change touching all 43 endpoints, whereas Y is under-built for both the decision and the security stakes.

The situation asks to first decide whether to migrate, then execute; Flow X's analyze:diagnose step makes that go/no-go decision Flow Y lacks, and its review step independently verifies a security-sensitive auth change touching all 43 endpoints.

The situation explicitly asks to first decide whether the migration is the right call, which the diagnose step in X provides and Y lacks; and touching all 43 auth endpoints is a high-blast-radius security change where X's reviewer step earns its place.

The situation requires the confirmed SQL-injection to be fixed in this same change, but Flow Y is read-only (no act, no run-verification) so it cannot deliver or prove the fix. Flow X's act + run-verification steps match the requirement to implement and verify the fix.

The situation requires the confirmed SQL-injection to be fixed in this same change, which needs the act:act(implementer) and verify:run-verification steps that only Flow X has. Flow Y is read-only (diagnose then review/close), so it would leave the requested fix unimplemented and unverified.

The task requires fixing the confirmed SQL-injection in this same change, but Flow Y is read-only with no act or run-verification step, so it cannot deliver or prove the fix. Flow X's act + run-verification steps are exactly what this confirmed-defect situation demands.
Flow X and Flow Y are identical step-for-step (frame, gather-context, plan, act, run-verification, review, close-with-evidence), so neither fits the situation better than the other.
Both flows are identical step-for-step (frame -> gather-context -> plan -> act -> run-verification -> review -> close-with-evidence), so neither has any edge for this situation.
Flow X and Flow Y are identical step-for-step (frame -> gather-context -> plan -> act -> run-verification -> review -> close-with-evidence), so neither can win on the merits.

Root cause is already pinned (single off-by-one at helpers.ts:42), so Flow Y's diagnose step is redundant work; Flow X goes straight to act + run-verification, which fits a known one-line fix with existing tests.
The diagnose step in Y is wasted work because the situation already names the exact root cause and location; X reaches the same fix-and-verify outcome without it.

The root cause is already pinned to one line (getMonthIndex off-by-one), so Flow Y's diagnose step is redundant ceremony; Flow X's act->verify->close is minimal-but-sufficient since the existing tests prove the fix.

The two flows are byte-identical (review-intake -> gather-context -> diagnose -> close-with-evidence), so neither can win on the merits; both are correctly read-only for this code-frozen security review.
Both flows are identical: review-intake -> gather-context -> diagnose -> close-with-evidence, a read-only shape that correctly omits act/verification per the "do not change code" constraint.
The two flows are identical step-for-step (review-intake -> gather-context -> diagnose -> close-with-evidence), and that read-only shape is exactly right for a no-code-change security review.
